subject: mesh-integrated mass properties of a body with a prescribed density field (rho = density * f(x)) against the closed block form fed with analytic mass properties
reference: Fossen (2011) eq. (3.44) closed block form + analytic mass properties

box_cases.name: box_homogeneous
box_cases.note: regression: the field path reproduces the pre-existing uniform arithmetic

box_cases.name: box_longitudinal
box_cases.note: fore-aft gradient: moves the CG by 2.0 m, leaves the mass unchanged

box_cases.name: box_vertical
box_cases.note: heavy-bottom gradient: moves the CG down, leaves the mass unchanged

barge_case.name: barge_production_vertical
barge_case.note: wetted barge hull closed by the waterplane = exact box; production entry mass_matrix_from_wetted_hull(density_field=...) vs the analytic box

ellipsoid_ladder.name: ellipsoid_sub2
ellipsoid_ladder.note: linear fore-aft density field on a curved hull

ellipsoid_ladder.name: ellipsoid_sub3
ellipsoid_ladder.note: linear fore-aft density field on a curved hull

ellipsoid_ladder.name: ellipsoid_sub4
ellipsoid_ladder.note: linear fore-aft density field on a curved hull

ellipsoid_ladder.name: ellipsoid_sub5
ellipsoid_ladder.note: linear fore-aft density field on a curved hull

negative_density.message: density_field must be positive on the body (min -1.02e+03 kg/m^3)

zero_density.message: density_field must be positive on the body (min 0 kg/m^3)

wrong_length.message: density_field must return one value per point: expected 48, got 3

verdict.criterion: M_RB from mesh-integrated inhomogeneous mass properties vs M_RB from analytic mass properties: affine density fields must agree to round-off (<1e-10) on the exactly polyhedral bodies, every accepted discretisation must be inside 3% (bilinear field on a refined box, linear field on a curved hull), both ladders must converge at second order (order > 1.5), the homogeneous limit must reproduce the pre-existing uniform route to 1e-12, and the field-ignoring control must exceed the 3% block tolerance on the cases where the field moves the CG or creates a product of inertia
